summary: A record-panel composition is drawn on the Sheet sheet: the variant that pushed this component past a navigation drawer. A row in a table opened beside it — Sheet.Header carrying Close plus record pagination and an open-the-full-record control, then Sheet.Body holding an identity block, a completeness hero, and an Accordion of field groups at size md. Nothing in it is a new part, which is the point: it exercises the size axis and the scrolling body the same day they shipped. Four decisions are recorded on the sheet with their evidence. The band stays CHROME and the identity scrolls, checked against the field rather than asserted — of six CRM detail panels surveyed on Mobbin, four pin one compact row and put the identity in the scrolling body (Twenty, Apollo, Lightfield, HubSpot) and one scrolls everything (folk); pinning a taller identity block is the minority pattern, and it would also miss the body's 16px lane by the 8 the band is inset. The hero is a COMPOSITION, not a component: Banner is the nearest thing and does not fit, being items-center with one text slot where this stacks a label row, a Progress at size sm, a consequence sentence and two controls. Field rows sit at px-xs inside the panel's px-sm, which is 4 + 8 = 12 and therefore the trigger's p-md exactly, so a group name and its fields share one lane; an empty value is an em dash in --ui-text-placeholder because a missing field and an unexamined one are different things and the meter above counts on the difference. And the chips are two different components that look alike: Disciplines and Tools are Badge neutral md (labels), while the hero's missing-field chips are Button secondary sm shape-full (controls) at 24px, which meets SC 2.5.8 exactly where Badge sm at 22px would not. CORRECTED on review: the field groups were first drawn as Accordion's PLAIN variant with hairline dividers between them, and both halves of that were wrong. A standard accordion has no border and no dividers — grouping is spacing alone, which is CONVENTIONS' own rule that a rule is a spacing problem solved with ink — so the hairlines were an invention. And plain has no hover either: the bg-hover step belongs to CARD, on the whole tile rather than the trigger, exactly as the Accordion sheet's Card States section labels it. Six pressable section headers on one surface is the case that needs it, so the panel is card now, radius-md tiles on bg-elevated at the root's own gap-xs, with Disciplines drawn hovered. That in turn took the fill off the hero: bg-elevated was the obvious answer and the card variant already owns it on the same surface, so the hero sits on the panel ground at the Body's own inset, where its text lane and the tiles' outer edges agree. The needsDesign row filed against Accordion is withdrawn — plain is not missing anything — and the two variants' real difference is recorded in accordion.doc.ts knownGaps instead: plain has no border, no dividers and no hover, card is a tile whose WHOLE surface answers the pointer, and a surface with pressable section headers wants card.
